title: The Climate Investment Trust
subtitle: Hold capital, lend its strength
message: Donors will not vote for large cash transfers. A trust that holds capital instead of spending it can take second loss behind policy guarantees: $5 billion supports about $54 billion of guarantees, and each donor dollar delivers 2.7–10 dollars of interest savings rather than one.

problem.text: Grants buy one project and are gone. Payments against counterfactual baselines reward delay. And sovereigns do not pay their peers, so an international feebate needs a trust to hold the pot.

mechanism.title: One pool, three jobs
mechanism.caption: A: interest savings per donor dollar. B: Trust capital over 25 years from $5bn at launch (stylized).
points: Second loss: the government first, the Trust second, a AAA entity last. A 9.3% buffer keeps exhaustion to 1% a year.
Investment: co-invest for 25% of private returns; regional funds hold first-loss tranches (Brief 2.2).
Accounts: credited by performance, pledgeable as collateral now, drawn after 2050.

action.title: Launch it as insurance first
results: $5bn ($1bn grants, $4bn country stakes) supports $54bn of guarantees, saving borrowers $1.6bn a year.
Insurance only, it must charge about 0.8% a year on exposure to hold steady.
$95bn of co-investment yields $2.4bn a year in fees: $18.5bn after 10 years, about $28bn in the long run.
